sections.title: AI eng vs ML eng vs full-stack

interview.q: How is AI engineering different from ML engineering?
Walk me through taking an LLM feature from prototype to production.

chapters.applyIt: Pick one feature in your own repo that could use an LLM. Write a one-page design doc covering the user problem, success metric, failure cost, a latency/cost budget, and a "non-LLM baseline". Use it as the running project for later chapters.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch1 (V); applied-llms.org https://applied-llms.org/ (K)

chapters.title: Text as Numbers: Tokenization

production.F: chat-template mismatch on self-hosted models; truncation mid-JSON.
production.C: non-English and code text costs 1.5–3× more tokens (verify per tokenizer).
production.O: log input/output/cached token counts per call.
production.S: special-token injection in user input.

interview.q: Why can't LLMs reliably count letters in "strawberry"?
How does BPE work?
Why does the same prompt cost different amounts across providers?
How would you estimate monthly token spend for a feature?

chapters.applyIt: Implement a minimal BPE trainer (about 100 lines). Then write a token-cost estimator that tokenizes 1,000 real inputs from your app with two tokenizers and projects monthly cost.
chapters.sources: CS336 Lecture 1 and Assignment 1 (V); Karpathy Zero to Hero https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html (K); mlabonne §1 (V)

production.F: mixing embeddings from two model versions in one index; domain mismatch.
production.C: re-embedding a corpus on model upgrade; storage per dimension.
production.L: query-embedding latency on the hot path.
production.O: track embedding model and version per vector.
production.S: embeddings can leak source text (inversion attacks).

interview.q: What is an embedding, and why does cosine similarity work?
Bi-encoder vs cross-encoder: when do you use each?
How would you pick an embedding model for legal documents?
How do you migrate 50M vectors to a new embedding model with zero downtime?

chapters.applyIt: Embed a sample of your own repo's docs or issues with two models. Build a 50-query labelled set and compare recall@10. Write a re-embedding migration plan (dual-write, backfill, cut-over).
chapters.sources: SLP3 https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/ (K); Chip Huyen Ch3 "Introduction to Embedding" (V); Sentence-BERT https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084 (K)

interview.q: What does temperature do mathematically?
Why is temperature 0 not fully deterministic?
How can you use log-probs for classification confidence?
Why do LLMs hallucinate, and what can engineering (not training) do about it?

chapters.applyIt: Write a sampling playground: implement temperature, top-k and top-p over raw logits from a small open model. Add a log-prob-based confidence threshold to a classifier in your app and measure precision at different thresholds.

chapters.title: Reasoning Models and Test-Time Compute

production.F: overthinking simple tasks; inconsistent effort.
production.C: thinking tokens billed as output, often several times the answer length.
production.L: TTFT of seconds to minutes; needs async UX.
production.O: log thinking-token counts separately.
production.S: reasoning traces may contain sensitive data; don't show them raw to users.

interview.q: When would you choose a reasoning model over a standard model?
How do you control cost with reasoning models?
Is chain-of-thought faithful?
Design a system that routes between fast and reasoning models.

chapters.applyIt: Take 50 tasks from your app. Run them at low, medium and high reasoning effort plus a non-reasoning model. Plot accuracy against cost and p50/p95 latency, then pick a routing policy.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch2 "Test Time Compute" (V); mlabonne "Test-Time Compute" (V); Berkeley F24 Denny Zhou (V); DeepSeek-R1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948 (K); Lilian Weng "Why We Think" https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2025-05-01-thinking/ (K)

sections.title: Prompt vs RAG vs fine-tune decision

production.F: catastrophic forgetting; overfitting to format; stale fine-tune versus improving base models.
production.C: training plus hosting a custom model; LoRA adapter multiplexing.
production.O: version datasets and adapters; eval before promotion.
production.S: training data leakage and PII memorization.

Explain LoRA. Why does it use so little memory?
How much GPU memory do you need to fine-tune a 7B model with QLoRA?
Design a distillation pipeline from a frontier model to a small model for classification.

chapters.applyIt: Distill a frontier model's outputs on one narrow task in your app (for example, ticket classification) into a LoRA on a small open model. Compare accuracy, cost per 1k calls and latency against the frontier model.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch7–8 (V); mlabonne §3–4, §7 (V); LoRA https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685 (K); QLoRA https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314 (K)

chapters.title: Inference Mechanics

production.F: OOM from KV cache at long context; quality loss from aggressive quantization.
production.C: GPU utilization drives the self-host cost; cached-input discounts.
production.L: TTFT vs throughput trade-off under batching.
production.O: track TTFT, ITL, tokens/s, queue depth, KV-cache utilization.
production.S: cross-tenant cache side channels.

interview.q: Explain the KV cache and why it is the memory bottleneck.
Why is decode memory-bandwidth-bound?
How does continuous batching improve throughput?
How does speculative decoding speed up generation without changing outputs?
Design an end-to-end batching system for LLM queries.

chapters.applyIt: Serve a small model with vLLM locally. Load-test it at concurrency 1 to 64, measuring TTFT, ITL and throughput. Then enable prefix caching and quantization and record the deltas.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch9 (V); CS336 Lecture 10 (V); mlabonne LLM Engineer §6 (V); PagedAttention https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180 (K); kipply https://kipp.ly/transformer-inference-arithmetic/ (K); "How to Scale Your Model" https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/ (K)

production.F: provider outage; 429 storms; silent model behaviour change on alias updates.
production.C: break-even between API and self-host.
production.O: per-provider error rates and spend.
production.S: vendor data-retention terms; key management.

interview.q: API or self-host for 10M requests/day? Walk through the math.
How do you choose a model for a new feature?
How do you make your app resilient to a provider outage?
How do you migrate safely when a model is deprecated?

chapters.applyIt: Put a gateway (LiteLLM-style or hand-rolled) in front of two providers in your app, with a fallback, retries with jitter, a per-feature cost tag and a model alias pinned to a version.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch4 and Ch10 (V); mlabonne "Running/Deploying LLMs" (V); Anthropic "Confidential Inference" (V); RouteLLM https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18665 (K)

chapters.title: Prompting Fundamentals

production.F: prompt regressions on model upgrades; few-shot overfitting; instruction conflicts.
production.C: bloated system prompts on every call (cache them).
production.O: prompt version ID on every trace.
production.S: secrets in system prompts are extractable.

interview.q: How do you systematically improve a prompt rather than by vibes?
Few-shot vs fine-tuning: trade-offs?
How do you version and roll out prompt changes safely?
Why might a prompt that worked on model A fail on model B?

chapters.applyIt: Move every prompt in your repo into versioned templates with IDs. Run one prompt through three iterations, each scored on a 30-example eval set (from Ch 19), and keep a changelog.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch5 (V); FSDL "Learn to Spell" (V); Berkeley F24 DSPy (V); Anthropic prompt docs https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview (K); Lost in the Middle https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172 (K)

chapters.title: Structured Output

production.F: valid-JSON-but-wrong-values; hallucinated enum values; schema drift.
production.C: retries double cost.
production.L: constrained decoding overhead; streaming partial JSON.
production.O: log validation failures by field.
production.S: treat model JSON as untrusted input (injection into SQL or shell).

interview.q: How do you guarantee valid JSON from an LLM?
How does constrained decoding work?
Design a document-extraction pipeline for 1M invoices/month, with accuracy SLAs.
How do you evaluate field-level extraction accuracy?

chapters.applyIt: Build an extractor for a real document type in your repos with a Pydantic schema, a repair loop and per-field accuracy metrics on 50 labelled docs.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch2 "Structured Outputs" (V); mlabonne (V); OpenAI Cookbook structured-output eval (S); Outlines https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09702 (K)

chapters.title: Multimodal and Realtime Voice

sections.title: Token costs of images and audio

production.F: OCR errors cascading; voice interruptions mishandled.

production.L: voice needs sub-~800 ms turn latency (verify against current vendor guidance).
production.O: per-stage latency (STT → LLM → TTS).
production.S: prompt injection via images; voice spoofing.

interview.q: Design a voice assistant for customer support.
How do you hit low latency in a voice agent?
How do you process scanned PDFs for RAG?

chapters.applyIt: Build a voice loop (STT → LLM → TTS) over one of your apps' APIs. Instrument per-stage latency and get p50 under your target.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch6 "RAG Beyond Texts" (V); mlabonne "Multimodal" (V); Latent Space Vision/Voice sections (V, headings only).

chapters.title: Information Retrieval Foundations

production.F: dense retrieval missing exact IDs or codes (needs BM25); ACL leaks.
production.C: re-ranker cost per query.

interview.q: BM25 vs dense retrieval: when does each win?
Why use hybrid search, and how does RRF work?
How do you measure retrieval quality without labels?
Where in the pipeline do you enforce document permissions?

chapters.applyIt: Index one of your repos' docs or issues with BM25 plus dense retrieval, add RRF and a cross-encoder, and report recall@10 and nDCG@10 for each stage on your 50-query set.
chapters.sources: Manning *Introduction to IR* https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/ (K); SLP3 (K); Chip Huyen Ch6 (V); DPR https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04906 (K); ColBERT https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.12832 (K)

pgvector or a dedicated vector DB?
Size the infrastructure for 100M 1024-dim vectors.
How do you handle deletes and GDPR erasure in a vector index?

chapters.title: RAG Pipelines

sections.title: RAG vs long context vs fine-tuning

production.F: the right doc exists but the answer is wrong (retrieval vs generation attribution); stale index; conflicting sources.
production.C: context tokens per query × QPS.
production.O: trace query → chunks → answer → citation.
production.S: indirect prompt injection via indexed documents; ACL-filtered retrieval.

interview.q: Design a production RAG system for 10M documents at 1K QPS.
The correct document exists but the answer is wrong. How do you debug it?
How do you choose a chunk size?
How do you handle conflicting information across sources?
Long context or RAG?

chapters.applyIt: Build a cited Q&A over your own repos (code plus READMEs) with incremental re-indexing on git push. Ship a "why this answer" trace view.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch6 (V); mlabonne RAG (V); FSDL askFSDL (V); RAG paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401 (K); Anthropic Contextual Retrieval https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval (K)

chapters.title: Advanced and Agentic RAG

production.F: agentic loops that never stop searching; text-to-SQL that writes destructive queries.
production.C: multi-hop multiplies calls.
production.L: iterative search runs to minutes, so needs async.
production.O: per-hop traces.
production.S: read-only DB roles for text-to-SQL; web content as an injection vector.

interview.q: When is agentic RAG worth its latency?
Design a text-to-SQL assistant for analysts. How do you make it safe?
Design a deep-research agent that produces a cited report.
Why do coding agents often prefer grep over vector search?

chapters.applyIt: Turn your Ch 17 RAG into an agent with `search_docs`, `grep_repo` and `read_file` tools. Compare it with single-shot RAG on multi-hop questions for accuracy, cost and latency.
chapters.sources: mlabonne "Advanced RAG" (V); Berkeley F24 Jerry Liu (V); Anthropic multi-agent research system (V); OpenAI Cookbook file and web search (S); PromptLayer (V)

chapters.title: Evals I: Methodology and Error Analysis

production.F: generic metrics ("helpfulness 4.2/5") that don't track real failures; eval sets that go stale.
production.C: eval runs cost tokens, so budget them.
production.O: evals are built from production traces.
production.S: eval data contains PII; handle it accordingly.

interview.q: How do you build an eval set for a new feature with no users yet?
What is error analysis, and how do you run it?
Model eval vs system eval: what's the difference?
How many examples do you need to detect a 5% regression?

chapters.applyIt: Review 100 real traces from your app and open-code the failures into a taxonomy. Turn the top three failure modes into a versioned eval set with pass/fail checks.
chapters.sources: Hamel Evals FAQ (V); Chip Huyen Ch3–4 (V); CS336 Lecture 12 (V); Anthropic "infrastructure noise" (V); Hamel "Your AI Product Needs Evals" https://hamel.dev/blog/posts/evals/ (K)

chapters.title: Evals II: Judges, RAG/Agent Evals and Continuous Evaluation

production.F: unvalidated judges; position and verbosity bias; flaky agent evals from environment noise.
production.C: a judge on every production trace is expensive, so sample.
production.O: dashboards of eval scores per release.
production.S: judge prompt injection by the outputs it grades.

interview.q: How would you evaluate an agent beyond its final answer?
How do you know your LLM judge is trustworthy?
Design an eval pipeline for a RAG chatbot, offline and online.
How do you put evals in CI without flaky failures?

chapters.applyIt: Build an LLM judge for your top failure mode, validate it against 100 human labels (report TPR/TNR), and wire it into GitHub Actions as a regression gate. Add trajectory assertions for one agent flow.
chapters.sources: Hamel FAQ (V); Chip Huyen Ch3 "AI as a Judge" (V); Anthropic "Demystifying evals for AI agents" and "Eval awareness" (V); Berkeley F25 Agent Evaluation (V); OpenAI Cookbook tools-evaluation (S); "Who Validates the Validators?" https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12272 (K); τ-bench https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045 (K)

chapters.title: Tool Use / Function Calling

production.F: wrong tool or args; huge tool outputs flooding context; duplicate side effects on retry.
production.C: tool definitions consume context on every call.
production.O: log every call, its args, result size and errors.
production.S: least privilege; validate arguments; never pass model-built strings to a shell or SQL unchecked.

interview.q: How does function calling work under the hood?
How do you design tools so the model uses them correctly?
A tool call charged a customer twice. What went wrong, and how do you prevent it?
How do you scale to 200 tools?

chapters.applyIt: Expose three real operations from one of your backends as tools, with idempotency keys, typed args, error messages written for the model, and a confirmation gate on writes. Measure tool-selection accuracy on 30 prompts.
chapters.sources: Anthropic "Writing effective tools" and "Advanced tool use" (V); Chip Huyen Ch6 "Tools" (V); OpenAI Cookbook function calling (S); Toolformer https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761 (K)

chapters.title: The Agent Loop and Architectures

production.F: infinite loops; goal drift; compounding errors; silent partial completion.
production.C: unbounded loops lead to runaway spend.
production.O: a per-step trace tree.
production.S: autonomy level matched to blast radius.

interview.q: Workflow or agent: how do you decide?
Implement a ReAct loop from scratch.
Design a support agent that drafts replies and escalates complex tickets.
How do you stop an agent from looping forever?
Framework or hand-rolled? Defend your choice.

chapters.applyIt: Hand-roll an agent loop (no framework) of about 200 lines with step and budget limits, checkpointing to disk and resume. Use it on one real workflow from your repos.
chapters.sources: Anthropic "Building effective agents" https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents (K), plus the two harness posts (V); Berkeley F24 Shunyu Yao and F25 Yann Dubois and Clay Bavor (V); Chip Huyen Ch6 (V); ReAct https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629 (K); Lilian Weng https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-06-23-agent/ (K); 12-factor agents https://github.com/humanlayer/12-factor-agents (K)

chapters.title: Memory

Design memory for a personal assistant used daily for a year.

chapters.title: Planning and Reasoning in Agents

production.F: over-planning; plans that are never revisited; unverifiable steps.

production.O: block and flag rates; appeal logs.
production.S: guardrails are defence in depth, not a security boundary.

How do you reduce hallucinations in production?

chapters.title: Observability

sections.title: Traces and spans for LLM calls

production.F: no way to reproduce a bad answer; silent quality drift after provider changes.
production.C: log storage of full prompts.
production.O: this chapter is the "O" for every other chapter.

What would you log for every LLM call?
Design observability for a multi-agent system.

chapters.title: Cost and Latency Engineering

production.F: semantic cache returning wrong answers; a cost spike from one runaway tenant.
production.C: this chapter is the "C" for every other chapter.
production.L: p95, not the mean; tail latency from long outputs.
production.O: cost per feature, tenant and model.
production.S: denial-of-wallet attacks; per-user rate limits.

interview.q: Our LLM bill tripled. Walk me through cutting it by 50% without hurting quality.
How does prompt caching work, and how do you design for it?
When is semantic caching dangerous?
Reduce p95 latency of a RAG chatbot from 6s to 2s.

chapters.applyIt: Build a cost/latency report for your app: cost per request by feature, then apply caching, routing and batch processing. Write a before/after table with quality held constant on your eval set.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch4, Ch9, Ch10 (V); Anthropic prompt caching docs https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching (K); RouteLLM (K).

chapters.title: Deployment and LLMOps

production.F: half-finished agent jobs on deploy; streaming connections dropped by proxies.
production.C: idle GPU capacity.
production.O: release markers on dashboards.
production.S: secrets management; sandbox isolation for agent runtimes.

interview.q: Design ChatGPT (or a chat product) end to end.
How do you roll out a new model version safely?
How do you serve long-running agent tasks behind an HTTP API?
Design an end-to-end architecture for an LLM app (gateway, cache, guardrails, router, observability).

chapters.applyIt: Deploy your app with streaming SSE, a job queue for long agent runs, a canary rollout of a new model version gated on eval scores, and shadow traffic.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch10 (V); FSDL LLMOps and "Launch in an Hour" (V); mlabonne "Deploying" (V); Anthropic "Scaling Managed Agents" (V); Chip Huyen "Building a GenAI Platform" https://huyenchip.com/2024/07/25/genai-platform.html (K)

chapters.title: Security: Prompt Injection and Agent Security

sections.title: OWASP LLM Top 10 and red teaming

production.F: an agent with private data access, untrusted input and an outbound channel, which is the lethal trifecta.
production.C: red-teaming cost.
production.O: audit logs of every tool action.
production.S: this chapter is the "S" for every other chapter.

interview.q: What is prompt injection, and why can't it be fully solved with filters?
An email assistant reads inbound mail and can send mail. Threat-model it.
How do you design an agent that safely browses the web?
Walk through the OWASP LLM Top 10.

chapters.applyIt: Red-team your own RAG/agent with 20 indirect-injection payloads planted in indexed docs. Then add the defences (tool allow-lists, egress blocking, no markdown-image rendering, approval on writes) and re-run.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch5 "Defensive Prompt Engineering" (V); mlabonne "Securing LLMs" (V); Berkeley F25 Safety and Security (V); Anthropic "Beyond permission prompts", "How we contain Claude", auto mode (V); Simon Willison https://simonwillison.net/series/prompt-injection/ (K); Greshake et al. https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12173 (K); CaMeL https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813 (K); OWASP https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/ (K)

chapters.title: Product UX for AI and the Feedback Loop

sections.title: Chat vs embedded vs ambient vs agentic UX

production.F: over-trust; users unable to correct the AI; dead-end refusals.
production.C: regenerate buttons multiply cost.
production.O: feedback events joined to traces.
production.S: UI rendering of model output (XSS, markdown exfiltration).

interview.q: How do you collect useful feedback without annoying users?
How would you measure whether an AI feature is succeeding?
Design the UX for an agent that takes irreversible actions.

chapters.applyIt: Add thumbs-plus-reason feedback, citation display, an undo/approval step and a progress stream to one feature. Join the feedback to traces and review a week of it.
chapters.sources: Chip Huyen Ch10 "User Feedback" (V); FSDL "UX for Language User Interfaces" (V); Google PAIR https://pair.withgoogle.com/guidebook/ (K); Microsoft HAX https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/haxtoolkit/ai-guidelines/ (K).
